dossier.architecture: Rear elevator/scorer with actively agitated serializer and cam-adjusted scoring geometry.

subsystems.intake: Station chute permits human-player tossing; collector/serializer geometry prioritizes a continuous path.
subsystems.transfer: Pre-Worlds rebuild replaced passive funnel/single belt with molded powered flaps that contact awkward coral in more orientations.
subsystems.scoring: Ladderator placement architecture; cam addition addressed week-1 L4 tipping and alignment delay. Roller locations revised to smooth handoff.
subsystems.endgame: Guide flap and cage locks; servo-dependent retention replaced by automatically engaging ratchet-like transmission so a partially completed climb survives disable.
subsystems.controls: Scoring and capture automation support shorter spot-to-score delay; exact full controls architecture not established here.

versions: Climb retention redesigned after lost climbs from late servo activation.
dossier.analysis: Passive funnels fail when a rigid pipe can sit where no powered surface touches it. The serializer rebuild is a general anti-jam lesson, while the climb revision addresses a separate deadline failure: securing the load before power disappears.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-3005 · A serializer rebuild must eliminate stable wrong orientations
context_documents.body:
# 2025-3005: A serializer rebuild must eliminate stable wrong orientations

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Before Worlds, passive polycarbonate funneling and one lower belt were replaced by molded powered flaps that contact awkward coral orientations. The retained ladder-style placement mechanism also received a cam after early L4 tipping/alignment difficulties. The interview separately describes a ratcheting climb that can retain partial progress after disable.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The serializer change is explicitly tied to coral settling into specific trapped orientations. Retaining a climb after power-off is described as an important requirement, not an incidental effect of gearing.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A funnel that succeeds in the common orientation can still create a stable mechanical equilibrium in an uncommon one. Powered flaps need to disturb that equilibrium without ejecting or crushing the piece. Likewise, an L4 scorer should be judged by placement stability and alignment delay, not only reaching the nominal height. These are distinct revisions and should not be attributed to one unchanging opening-week robot.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Deliberately place coral in every previously trapped pose, measure recovery time, and test L4 placement after abrupt chassis stops. Verify retention with the actual disabled climb configuration.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/oTLDniUNgBQ](https://youtu.be/oTLDniUNgBQ)

source_reviews.title: RoboChargers Relay CAD release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team-authored release and technical replies.
facts: Team chose continuous chain largely from familiarity. Coral ejector used carbon tube and MaxComposite. Reef contact could derail the laterator. The team shimmed lateral play before offseason use. Hard-stop parts changed from Onyx to MaxComposite for weight. As-built bumper spacers were omitted from CAD.
source_reviews.limitations: Release includes links to models. Assemblies were not dimensionally audited.

source_reviews.title: RoboChargers Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read older dossier synopsis. Full captions not retrieved.
facts: Retained account describes pre-Worlds powered serializer rebuild, cam revision for L4 and a climb retention redesign.
source_reviews.limitations: Separate evidence tier from release replies.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Relay uses a station-fed coral path into a moving scorer. The strongest new evidence concerns what happened when the scoring end contacted the reef. The team reports that the carbon tube and composite ejector carried tensile load through such incidents, while the laterator could derail and eventually needed shimming. That points to a real distinction between a strong end effector and a robust sliding interface. A mechanism can survive a collision materially and still lose the registration needed to score.
piece_flow: Station chute accepts coral. The retained account describes a move from passive funnel with single belt to powered molded flaps.
The serializer orients coral and passes it to the raised or positioned scorer. The cam's exact linkage and event versions need confirmation.
For endgame the retained synopsis describes guide-and-lock capture, revised to secure a partial climb if disable arrived.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A station opening, chain elevator and movable ejector share one envelope. Electrical routing was handled in the team's block CAD workflow. The published bumper gap was intended to make installation easier and relies on spacers omitted from the model, a concrete case where measuring the nominal CAD alone could misstate the contact geometry.

subsystems.name: Serializer
subsystems.construction: Powered molded flaps in the retained pre-Worlds description. The CAD reply separately identifies a PLA sprocket in a low-torque application.
subsystems.operation: Keep contact on coral that arrives outside the nominal orientation and feed the output at the scorer's loading height.
subsystems.team_rationale: The old synopsis links the revision to awkward coral positions that escaped the passive funnel's powered region.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Map every stable pipe pose in the channel. If a pipe can rest without contact, raising roller speed at the outlet will not recover it. Confirm that adding a flap does not create a new pinch point.
subsystems.interfaces: Chute exit, roller contact and scorer load pose need overlap across actual feed angles.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test reverse clearing and replacement of compliant contacts. Keep the printed sprocket evidence tied to its low-load role.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact powered contact geometry and relation of 7A12 sprocket to the serializer.

subsystems.name: Chain elevator and ejector
subsystems.construction: Continuous chain elevator, carbon-tube and composite ejector, and laterator in team replies. The old dossier adds the scoring cam.
subsystems.operation: Raise and place coral. The retained account links the cam to early L4 stability and alignment work.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team cites chain familiarity and weight reduction for revised stops.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Contact loads can bend or unseat the guide even when the tube survives. Track both lateral play and vertical position drift at the scorer. Keep composite edges out of concentrated bearing contact unless the joint distributes load.
subsystems.interfaces: Coral ejector, reef, lateral guide and chain lift can become one load path during contact.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect after reef contact, check guide retention and remeasure lateral play. Track hard-stop deformation across cycles.
subsystems.unknowns: Reef load and shim dimensions, cam geometry and exact stop installation.

subsystems.name: Climb
subsystems.construction: Guide flap and cage locks in retained interview synopsis. Later retention is described as automatically engaging.
subsystems.operation: Capture and lift before disable, with retention entering as load is acquired.
subsystems.team_rationale: Old dossier links revision to climbs lost when a separate servo activated too late.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Treat power loss mid-sequence as an explicit load case. A passive catch can protect partial progress if it engages throughout useful travel.
subsystems.interfaces: Guide and cage must clear station structure and scorer. Retention should carry load without motor torque.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test interruption at first load, mid-stroke and final hold. Check how to unload a caught mechanism safely.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual retention architecture and test history.

revisions: Team reports shimming the laterator before offseason play and replacing Onyx hard stops with lighter composite. Serializer, cam and climb changes are inherited from the interview synopsis.
transferable_principles: Measure retained guide engagement after contact, not just survival of the structure.
Record as-built spacers and wear adjustments alongside release CAD.
disconfirming_conditions: An active serializer can lose its benefit if the upstream chute already presents consistent orientation.
Chain familiarity can be outweighed by mass, lubrication and maintenance requirements in a different lift.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, exact cam and cage lock geometry, and dated competition configurations.
